title: Bhutan Tour Package From Siliguri
highlights: Spend a wonderful time in Bhutan as you experience its culture & traditions while exploring the top attractions of Thimphu and Paro.
Stand beneath the immense 177 ft Buddha Dordenma in Thimphu, a peaceful symbol offering spectacular panoramic views of the Thimphu Valley.
Visit Motithang Takin Preserve, home to Bhutan’s rare national animal, the Takin, in a 8-acre sanctuary surrounded by lush hills.
Hike to the iconic Tiger’s Nest Monastery, perched on a cliffside, where Guru Padmasambhava meditated in the sacred caves in the 8th century.
Explore Bhutan’s history at Ta Dzong, a 17th-century watchtower turned national museum, where ancient artefacts tell the story of Bhutan’s rich heritage.
overview:
About the tour:
Begin your expedition with our Bhutan Tour Package from Siliguri to the enchanting town of Phuentsholing. Feel the vibrant culture of Thimphu and the tranquility of Paro. The climax of your journey is the awe-inspiring excursion to Taktsang, the Tiger's Nest Monastery perched majestically on a cliffside. Opt for this package to connect with Bhutan on a personal level, where every moment becomes a cherished part of your travel story. Join us on this adventure to feel the vibrant vibe of Bhutan.
inclusions: 2 nights stay in Phuntsholing with breakfast and lunch or dinner
1 night stay in Thimphu City with breakfast and lunch or dinner
Thimphu Sightseeing Tour with Simtokha Dzong
2 nights stay in Paro with breakfast and lunch or dinner
exclusions: Meals not mentioned in the itinerary or inclusions
know_before_you_go: Ask your local guide to help you purchase a SIM on arrival, as Bhutan supports 2 networks: B-Mobile SIM and TashiCell.
Images are for representation purpose only.

ID Proof is mandatory for each individual guest at the time of booking, and upon arrival. PAN Card will not be considered as a valid identity proof. All foreign nationals must carry their passport as a proof of identity.

Indians must pay the Sustainable Development Fee (SDF) of Rs 1200 per person/per night. Children below 5 years are exempted from SDF, while kids between 6 and 12 years of age, will get 50% concession.
To obtain entry in Bhutan, Indian tourists must carry their passports with a minimum 6 months validity and make the payment of SDF.
Plastic has been banned since 1999 in Bhutan, therefore, it is advised to carry plastic/plastic items.
Keep your arms and legs covered while visiting a Dzong (fortress-monastery).
Ask for permission from the attending authority before taking any photos or videos inside places like monasteries.
In Bhutan, Tuesday is ‘Dry Day’. This means locals don’t drink alcohol on Tuesday. So it would be respectful to avoid alcohol on Tuesdays too.
It’s illegal for tobacco to be sold in Bhutan. Tourists can bring cigarettes into the country, but can only smoke them in designated places.
Bhutan does not have a micro (or nano) SIM card. So check your mobile device for SIM compatibility before visiting Bhutan.
Credit cards are widely accepted in major cities and tourist areas. However, it is recommended to carry some cash.
The official currency in Bhutan is the Bhutanese Ngultrum (BTN). It is advisable to exchange currency at banks or authorised exchange bureaus.

meal_plans.name: Bermuda Plan
meal_plans.description: The Bermuda meal plan offers three meals at select restaurants, including breakfast, lunch, and dinner along with drinks included. Ideal for a hassle-free, all-inclusive dining experience.

meal_plans.name: Dinner Plan
meal_plans.description: The Dinner Plan provides guests with two meals included in their stay: breakfast and dinner.

meal_plans.name: American Plan
meal_plans.description: It includes all three major meals, breakfast, lunch, and dinner for the length of your stay. Generally, the rates on this plan are higher but offer a good value for your money, and of course, added convenience.

meal_plans.name: Modified American Plan
meal_plans.description: Also known as Half Board or Half Pension meal plan. It is a modified version of the American Plan and includes a room stay with breakfast and a choice between lunch and dinner.

meal_plans.name: Continental Plan
meal_plans.description: It is where your room stay involves a daily breakfast at the hotel. The hotel can either affix its option of breakfast menu or provide in the dining area for a buffet breakfast. Also, whether the room service provides the breakfast or in a general dining area, depends from hotel to hotel.

meal_plans.name: European Plan
meal_plans.description: Only the stay is included in the rates and that you will have to pay extra for using the hotel’s dining facilities. This can be called the “Room Only” Plan.

days.title: Arrival in Siliguri | Transfer to Phuntsholing | Leisure Day
days.desc: Upon arrival at Siliguri Railway Station/Bagdogra Airport, get driven to the hotel in Phuntsholing. After check in, spend the rest of the day at leisure. You can explore the Bhutan Gate with its intricate architecture, or visit Zangto Pelri, which houses eight life-sized idols of different manifestations of Guru Padmasambhava (also called Guru Rinpoche). You can also visit Karbandi Monastery, one of Bhutan's oldest monasteries, nestled in the hills. Later, return to the hotel on your own.

days.title: Transfer to Thimphu | Leisure Day
days.desc: Check out and get driven to the immigration office to obtain the travel permit. Continue your journey to the hotel in Thimphu. En route, stop at Chukha dam & marvel at Bhutan’s largest hydropower project. Once you reach Thimpu, check in and enjoy the day at leisure. You can explore various sites such as the Clock Tower Square, National Institute For Zorig Chusum, Ludrong Memorial Garden and more. Later, return to the hotel for an overnight stay.

days.title: Thimphu Sightseeing Tour | Transfer to Paro
days.desc: Today, check out of the hotel & board your transfer for a sightseeing tour of Thimphu. Admire the National Memorial Chorten, a stupa commemorating Bhutan’s third king. Visit the Motithang Takin Preserve to see Bhutan's national animal. Also, marvel at the impressive Tashichho Dzong, a fortress-monastery that houses thirty temples, chapels and shrines. Explore other sites such as Simply Bhutan Museum & Changangkha Monastery. Later, get driven to Paro & upon arrival, check in to your hotel.

days.title: Hike to Tiger’s Nest Monastery
days.desc: Today, get driven to the Tiger’s Nest parking lot. From there, begin your 7 km hike to the iconic Taktsang Monastery. Ascend through lush pine forests adorned with colourful prayer flags. Inside the monastery, explore prayer wheels, meditation caves, and murals dedicated to Guru Rinpoche. Marvel at the breathtaking views from this sacred site, perched dramatically on a cliffside at 3,120 meters above sea level. After the descent, get transferred back to the hotel for an overnight stay.

days.title: Transfer to Phuntsholing | Leisure Day
days.desc: Today, check out and get transferred to Phuntsholing. Upon arrival, check in to your hotel and enjoy the day at leisure. You can visit various sites such as Tashi Chholing Shedra, known for its Buddhist learning center, and Alapan's View Point, offering panoramic views. Additionally, you can take a relaxing stroll by the Torsa River, famous for its scenic beauty, or explore the vibrant Phuntsholing Market for local crafts and souvenirs. Later, return to the hotel for an overnight stay.
